subject: Electrolytes
title: Hyponatremia: Osmolality, Symptoms and Safe Correction
preview: A stepwise approach separates true hypotonic hyponatremia from translocational or analytical explanations.

sections.title: Classify by effective osmolality
points: Hyperglycemia can lower measured sodium through water shifts; this differs from true hypotonic water excess.
Normal measured osmolality in an unexpected low sodium result raises the possibility of a measurement-related problem in selected settings.

sections.title: Identify the physiology
points: Volume status, renal concentrating response, diuretics, endocrine disease and fluid intake guide the differential.
Management is tailored to symptoms, chronicity, clinical status and measured repeat values.

sections.title: Exam trap — correction is not a race
points: Severe neurological symptoms require emergency supervised management; mild longstanding cases need a different pathway.
Correction can accelerate unexpectedly after the cause resolves, making frequent monitoring essential.

quickRevision: First evaluate neurological symptoms and measured serum osmolality; do not classify hyponatremia from the sodium number alone.
After confirming hypotonic hyponatremia, assess volume status, medication causes and urine osmolality/sodium.
Overly rapid correction of chronic hyponatremia can cause osmotic demyelination.

quiz.question: What is the feared consequence of overly rapid correction of chronic hyponatremia?
quiz.explanation: Rapid correction of chronic hypotonic hyponatremia increases the risk of osmotic demyelination syndrome; safe correction requires repeated sodium and clinical assessment.
